scenes.headline: What comes out when agents turn plans into 3D
scenes.sub: Snaptrude, Interior AI, a barn renovation and 3d-new-era-ai
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jamb! Four tools turned floor plans into buildings this week. Let's sort them by what comes out.

scenes.credit: videos from the posts on X

steps.say: DWG sheets into a hotel. A plan image into a flat. A vector PDF into a barn.

steps.caption: Read from a vector PDF, no AI
steps.say: All of it looks like 3D. It is not the same kind of thing.

scenes.title: What a plan says, and leaves out

legend: The plan gives footprints: axes, thicknesses, openings
Heights are not on the plan: a default
Openings as elements: a hole, a sill, a lintel
Traced from pixels: gaps up to 130 cm become wall
Wider gaps: a hole from floor to top

steps.say: A plan is a cut through the building, looking down. It gives footprints, thicknesses, and openings.

steps.term: Default: a value the tool fills in
steps.say: It gives no heights. So every tool fills them in: a default, a setting, a prompt, or a guess.
A building model cuts each door and window into its host wall, with a sill and a lintel.
Trace the plan from pixels, and a door is a break in a dark band. Short gaps become solid wall.
A wide one leaves a hole from floor to top. Either way, the openings are gone.

scenes.credit: Snaptrude's demo, from its post on X

steps.say: Snaptrude's typed request is one line. The brief behind it gives the storey heights: three point four and four metres.

steps.caption: Two questions a plan cannot answer
steps.say: Its two questions are ones a plan cannot answer. It claims IFC. The demo never opens one.

scenes.credit: Interior AI's panel, from levelsio's video

steps.say: Interior AI says it plainly. Sizes are estimates. One floor only.

scenes.credit: Romain Briaux's barn tool, from his post on X

steps.say: The barn tool reads the vector drawing. Each storey has a ceiling height and a slab.

steps.caption: Width over height: 74/204
steps.say: French plans write each opening's height on the sheet, so it reads that too.

scenes.credit: Romain Briaux's barn tool, from his post on X

steps.say: Walls are layered build-ups with R values. The richest model here, and no export yet.
3d-new-era-ai is open source, so I ported its wall tracer and ran it on levelsio's plan. Every door became wall.

steps.caption: Gaps of 60, 61, 81, 92 and 92 cm bridged
steps.say: And the glassy living room walls vanished, the same ones Interior AI missed.
So what comes out? Snaptrude claims IFC.
Interior AI gives you a scene to walk and paint.
The barn tool, nothing yet.
3d-new-era-ai keeps real walls inside, and exports one mesh.

scenes.text: Every plan-to-3D tool invents the vertical half. Ask where each height came from.

No heights on a plan, doors traced into walls, and one IFC claim to check. Thanks for watching!
